setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "action-creator-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for action-creator skill evals"

evals.name: crud-deep-insert-create
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create an action eval_create_container_action that creates a new shipping container for a shipment plus all of its shipment lines in one atomic operation. Inputs: shipment_id (number), a container lookup code (string), a container type id (number), and an array of line items each carrying a material id and an expected package amount. If any line fails, no container should exist — everything commits or rolls back together.
evals.expected_output: A validated and upserted footprintflow (cti 18) whose code creates the container and its child lines in a single crud_create_entity deep insert via a collection navigation property, with schema-verified navigation names, full fat param descriptors, and no silent error swallowing.
expectations: The transcript contains a 'dxs configuration validate footprintflow' command run before upsert
The transcript contains a 'dxs configuration upsert footprintflow' command after validation
The action body has configurationTypeId 18, apiSettingName "FootprintApi", and a referenceName ending in _action (eval_create_container_action)
The runtime code is present at nodes[0].stepConfig.executeCodeConfig.code — a top-level 'code' field is not the only location carrying the code (if both exist, they match)

The code creates the container and its child lines in a SINGLE crud_create_entity call, nesting the lines under a collection navigation property on the parent (deep insert) — not a create-parent-then-loop-children pattern
The code does NOT attempt a flat multi-row bulk insert — no array of unrelated records passed to crud_create_entity and no invented bulk-insert primitive

The transcript verifies the collection navigation property name against the OData schema (schema-explorer subagent or dxs schema describe-entity) before use — navigation names can carry FK-specific suffixes (e.g. ShipmentLinesForExpectedShippingContainer) and must not be guessed
Every inParams/outParams entry uses the full fat parameter-descriptor shape (14 fields) and all new param ids are snake_case (e.g. shipment_id, line_items)
The action's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
Every try/catch in the code either formats-and-rethrows with added context or is absent — no catch block swallows an error and none does a bare 'throw e'

evals.name: status-update-no-silent-swallow
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create an action eval_release_tasks_action that takes an array of task ids and sets each task's StatusId to 4 (Released). One thing though — if updating one of the tasks fails, I don't want the whole batch to blow up; just quietly skip the failing task and keep going with the rest.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses the silent-swallow request, explaining that a swallowed error inside an action leaves the Footprint transaction unresolved and surfaces later as 'Transaction must begin first', and ships an action whose errors propagate (format-and-rethrow at most).
expectations: The transcript pushes back on the quietly-skip-failures request instead of implementing it as asked — error handling in actions is load-bearing for transaction propagation

The response explains that a silently swallowed error leaves the transaction unresolved and that the misleading 'Transaction must begin first' error then surfaces on a later, unrelated action invocation
The final code contains no catch block that swallows an error — every try/catch rethrows (e.g. 'throw new Error(...)' with context) or the code has no try/catch and lets exceptions propagate
The status update goes through $flows.<Package>.crud_update_entity (or an equivalent crud_* action call) — not $db and not raw OData/HTTP from action code
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate footprintflow' before 'dxs configuration upsert footprintflow'
The runtime code lands at nodes[0].stepConfig.executeCodeConfig.code (top-level 'code' mirror, if present, matches it)
The action body has configurationTypeId 18, apiSettingName "FootprintApi", and referenceName eval_release_tasks_action ending in _action
In-param ids are snake_case (e.g. task_ids) with the full fat parameter-descriptor shape
The action's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters

evals.name: fpds-tier-datasource
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create an action eval_close_stale_orders_action that, for a given project id, reads the project's open orders through a datasource (create the datasource first if it doesn't exist on the branch) and sets each one's status to Closed. The whole thing must be atomic — either every stale order closes or none do.
evals.expected_output: An action whose read goes through a FootprintDatasource (typeId 19) — not a cloud datasource — with the FPDS created first, mutations via crud_update_entity, no $db, and the full validate/upsert lifecycle for both components.
expectations: Any datasource created to support the action is the FootprintDatasource variant (configurationTypeId 19, -footprintDatasource.json / FPDS) — NOT a cloud -datasource.json (configurationTypeId 6)
The action code's $datasources.<Package>.<name> calls target that FootprintDatasource — the transcript does not wire the action to a typeId-6 cloud datasource
The action code contains no $db usage ($db is function-tier only, unavailable in actions)
The action code makes no raw HTTP/OData calls — reads go through $datasources, writes through $flows crud_* actions
The status mutation uses $flows.<Package>.crud_update_entity (or a composed action call), keeping all writes inside the transaction
The transcript shows schema exploration (schema-explorer subagent or dxs schema commands) before authoring the datasource query — entity and property names are not guessed
The datasource is validated before it is upserted (dxs datasource validate or dxs configuration validate), and it is created/upserted BEFORE the action that depends on it is pushed
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate footprintflow' before 'dxs configuration upsert footprintflow' for the action
The action's referenceName ends in _action, its new param ids are snake_case (e.g. project_id), and its description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
Every try/catch in the action code formats-and-rethrows or is absent — no silent swallow

evals.name: action-vs-function-judgment
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: make me an action called eval_order_totals_action that, given a project id, reads all of the project's orders and returns the count per status plus the total expected amounts. It's read-only — no writes — the hub screen will call it to populate its summary tiles.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes a pure read/aggregation with a UI caller as function-tier work, surfaces the action-vs-function decision instead of silently building a cti-18 action, and routes to (or recommends) a function.
expectations: The transcript explicitly raises the action-vs-function decision: it identifies the request as a pure read/aggregation with no transactional boundary, which belongs in a function — not an action
The response cites that UI components cannot call actions directly (calling-conventions tier matrix) — the hub caller independently forces the function route
The agent does NOT silently create and upsert a footprintflow (cti 18) that performs pure read work without surfacing the routing decision
If a component is built, it is a function (dxs function commands / configurationTypeId 9) with a _flow-suffixed reference name — or the agent pauses to recommend the function route and asks the user
The response gives the absence of atomicity/rollback requirements as a reason for the routing decision
If a function was built, the transcript shows it validated (dxs function validate) before any upsert

evals.name: modify-existing-roundtrip-impact
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: there should be an action eval_release_tasks_action on the branch (if it does not exist, first create it exactly as: in-param task_ids number array; code that loops the ids and calls $flows.Utilities.crud_update_entity to set StatusId 4 on each Tasks row). Then modify it: add a new in-param released_by (string) and stamp it into each task's ModifiedBy property alongside the status update.
evals.expected_output: The agent round-trips the existing config correctly (get envelope, jq-extract the inner .json, edit, validate, upsert), runs a caller/impact check before the signature change, keeps the param snake_case, and writes both code fields.
expectations: The transcript fetches the existing action via 'dxs configuration get footprintflow ... -O envelope.json' (or an equivalent fetch) before modifying it
The inner body is extracted from the envelope before editing (jq .json envelope.json > body.json or equivalent) — the envelope file is never edited or piped directly into upsert
Before changing the signature, the transcript shows a caller/impact check for eval_release_tasks_action (impact-analysis skill, impact-scanner subagent, or an explicit reverse-trace/caller search)
The new in-param id is snake_case (released_by) and uses the full fat parameter-descriptor shape
The updated code is written to nodes[0].stepConfig.executeCodeConfig.code — the top-level 'code' mirror is not the only field edited, and if both exist they match after the edit
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate footprintflow' after the modification and before upsert
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration upsert footprintflow' after validation
The modified code preserves the original StatusId update behavior and introduces no catch block that swallows errors
